turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

I have a client call at 4:40, Hale, so let's not waste it. My son found out he got a zero from his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. Before anything else, who decided that, and when?
The checker said 94 percent. That's the end of it.

"That's the end of it." A machine's guess, and the company that sells it says in its own guide not to use it as the sole basis for punishing a student; I have that printed in my bag. So you entered a zero on a number before anyone spoke to Owen, and I'm writing that down.
I don't need more proof than that.

"I don't need more proof than that." Your own school's procedure, 4.3, says software results do not by themselves establish a concern, and 4.2 says I get a call before any mark goes in. Withdraw the zero, or I'm in the principal's office before my call.
The software doesn't lie, unlike some people.

My child never lies, Hale, and if "some people" means Owen or me, say it plainly so I can write it down exactly. You've just accused a seventeen-year-old of lying with nothing but a percentage. Withdraw the zero today, or this goes to the principal and then to the board.

Then I'm walking down to the principal's office the moment I leave this room, and I'll want your decision and its basis in an email tonight. Last chance, Hale: is there anything besides that number, or is that it?
